title: Token Cost Attribution and Explainable Trace Playbook
author: Riya Nandakumar
body:
Summary:

This playbook documents the platform approach for token-level cost attribution and explainable traces through the inference stack. It defines dashboards, alerts, queries, and a step-by-step investigation and mitigation runbook for token-cost anomalies and regressions. The goal is to provide deterministic, auditable explanations for cost changes down to request and model-variant level so product teams and SREs can act quickly.

Why this matters:
- Token costs are the dominant operational variable for LLM inference. Small per-token regressions compound quickly.
- Root causes often cross layers: prompt changes, model variant selection, batching configuration, KV cache misses, or routing fallbacks.
- Observability that ties tokens -> request metadata -> model variant -> runtime path is required for targeted remediation and accurate customer billing.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: Platform SREs, Runtime Engineers, Cost Ops, Product owners for high-volume endpoints.
- Scope: Hosted + Dedicated inference paths; Private deployments should mirror instrumentation via the same schema. Does NOT include offline training costs.

Definitions:
- token_event: single emitted token record including model_variant, request_id, client_key, latency_bucket, cost_unit.
- explain_trace_id: deterministic id connecting an HTTP request through routing, batching, and GPU execution shards.
- effective_cost_per_token (ECPT): normalized cost metric after batching and amortized KV cache credit.

High-level design:
1) Instrumentation: insert token_event emitters at two points: (a) post-generation in the runtime (per-token metadata), (b) router/gateway that records request metadata and selected model_variant. Both share explain_trace_id.
2) Aggregation pipeline: events flow to Kafka -> materialized into a short-term OLAP (ClickHouse) and long-term cube (Druid/BigQuery) for cost analytics.
3) Dashboards: a set of Grafana panels that join request metadata and token_event aggregates to produce explainable cost breakdowns.
4) Alerting: SLO-driven alerts for delta in ECPT and token-volume-weighted model fallback rates.

Dashboards and panels (owner: platform-observability):
| Panel | Primary metric | Target | Notes |
| ---- | ---- | ---- | ---- |
| ECPT overview | 24h rolling ECPT | < baseline +5% | Spotlight by model_family |
| Explainable trace explorer | sample traces by explain_trace_id | interactive | linkable from incidents |
| Model-variant fallback heatmap | fallback_rate per region | <1% | per-hour granularity |
| KV cache hit-rate vs ECPT | hit_rate | >90% | stratified by prefix |

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- ecpt_delta_1h: trigger when ECPT increases >7% vs 7-day baseline and token_volume_1h > 10k.
- fallback_surge: trigger when model_variant_fallback_rate_10m > 2% AND affected_routes > 3.
- cache-degradation: KV cache hit_rate_15m drops >15% AND corresponding ECPT increases.

Investigation runbook (on-call SRE):
1) Triage from PagerDuty alert: record alert id and time.
2) Open Explainable Trace Explorer and select top-10 traces by ECPT delta.
3) Identify common attributes: request route, model_variant, region, client_key, sequence_length_bucket.
4) Correlate with deploys: check deployments in the last 60 minutes (CI/CD pipeline).
5) Check runtime metrics: batch_size distribution, GPU utilization, KV cache hit/miss heatmap.
6) If fallback_surge: inspect routing logs for capacity errors or API quota nodes. Rollback routing rule if necessary.
7) If cache-degradation: trigger cache warmup and re-evaluate batch policies.
8) Communicate: post status in incident channel with a one-line cause hypothesis and mitigation steps.

Mitigation play actions (ordered by impact and reversibility):
1) Apply tiered throttling to low-priority tenants to restore ECPT for critical routes.
2) Switch high-latency routes to a lower-cost cached model_variant for a rolling 5-minute window.
3) Reconfigure batch_max_latency to avoid pathological micro-batches (runtime flag: --batch-max-ms).
4) Evict stale KV prefixes if hit_rates show long-tail pollution.

Ownership and escalation:
- First responder: platform-oncall (SRE).
- Secondary: runtime-team (kernel/scheduler owner).
- Escalation: head of platform within 60 minutes if user-impacting costs persist or SLAs are breached.

Implementation notes: sample instrumentation and queries
- Example ClickHouse insert (simplified):
INSERT INTO token_events (ts, explain_trace_id, request_id, client_key, model_variant, token_count, token_cost, kv_hit) VALUES (...);

- Sample ClickHouse aggregation query for ECPT by model_variant:
SELECT model_variant, sum(token_cost) / sum(token_count) AS ecpt, countDistinct(request_id) AS requests
FROM token_events
WHERE ts BETWEEN subtractHours(now(), 1) AND now()
GROUP BY model_variant
ORDER BY ecpt DESC
LIMIT 20;

- Prometheus / Alertmanager (conceptual) PromQL examples:
ecpt_delta = (sum(rate(token_cost_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(token_count_sum[5m])))
alert: ECPTIncrease
expr: ecpt_delta / (avg_over_time(ecpt_delta[7d])) > 1.07 and sum(rate(token_count_sum[1h])) > 10000
for: 10m

Runbook play examples for automation (playbook scripts):
- automated-mitigation: on ECPTIncrease, run a canary re-route for 5% of traffic to stable-model-001, notify on call and open MR to revert if stable.

Rollout and guardrails:
1) Feature-flag dashboard rollout: start with platform-internal only for 72 hours.
2) Telemetry completeness gate: require >=99% of explain_trace_id presence across router + runtime for a 48h window.
3) Read-only export: provide product teams a daily CSV of ECPT by route for billing reconciliation.

Post-incident retrospective checklist:
- Timestamped timeline of signals and actions (10-minute resolution).
- Root cause summary with evidence (traces, queries, deploy diff).
- Cost impact estimate (USD/day) and affected customers list.
- Action items with owners and due dates (e.g., instrumentation gaps, 1-week follow-up).

Appendix: quick debugging commands and common failure patterns
- Common patterns and likely causes:
  * Single route spike with stable fallback rate -> suspect prompt/usage change from a customer.
  * Global ECPT increase + batch size drop -> suspect upstream throttling or backend cold starts.
  * ECPT increase with KV miss spike -> model or prefix mis-routing or cache eviction policy change.

- Useful queries and flags:
  * Get recent traces for a request_id: SELECT * FROM token_events WHERE request_id = '<id>' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 500;
  * Dump a sample explainable trace: platform-cli trace get --id <explain_trace_id> --format json
  * Runtime flags to inspect: --batch-max-ms, --kv-cache-window-seconds, --quantize-profile-id

Related work and next steps:
- Integrate explainable traces with alert annotations to automatically attach root-cause candidates.
- Add model-variant cost-simulations to the Console so product owners can forecast ECPT before rollouts.
- Expand long-term retention of per-request traces for monthly billing audits (cost/space tradeoff).

Contacts and ownership:
- Document owner: platform-observability@redwood.com
- On-call rotation: see /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/platform-regional-capacity-matrix-and-shifthandoff-handbook-2024 for current oncall roster.

This playbook is intended to be updated iteratively. If you find gaps in instrumentation or analysis, add a follow-up action to the retrospective section and assign it to the runtime or platform-observability team.
